explanation: The statement is entirely about library-specific objects: `size` (an essential-supremum norm defined in this file via `eLpNorm _ ∞ phaseVolume`), `PositiveIntegral.value`, `PositiveIntegral.time`, `PositiveIntegral.time_idempotent`, `PositiveIntegral.time_bounds` and `JetBarrier.flight`. Its mathematical content is that the composition `t ↦ size (fun p => f (t,p))` of a mild solution is continuous on ℝ, obtained by reindexing along the transport `PositiveIntegral.time` (the library lemma `time_idempotent` and `time_bounds` are used for this) and then applying the library lemma `continuousOn_size` together with `ContinuousOn.comp_continuous`. I searched Mathlib for candidates: `ContinuousOn.comp_continuous` (Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousOn.lean) is the generic glue lemma only, and greps for `continuousOn_size`/`size` return nothing in Mathlib outside this library — Mathlib has no notion of `phaseVolume`, `size`, `PositiveIntegral.value` or `time`, so no Mathlib declaration states this result, and it is not a one-step instantiation of any Mathlib theorem.
